note: Literature directly supports that dominant-negative MH2 domain missense variants in SMAD3 correlate with earlier major aortic events and altered vascular smooth muscle/fibroblast differentiation compared to haploinsufficient variants, though some earlier cohorts observed no categorical correlation.

evidence.text: Individuals carrying dominant-negative SMAD3 variants in the MH2 domain experienced more major events at an earlier age compared to individuals with haploinsufficient variants, accompanied by differential myofibroblast differentiation and extracellular matrix production.

source.title: Functional analysis of cell lines derived from SMAD3-related Loeys-Dietz syndrome patients provides insights into genotype-phenotype relation
source.quote: Individuals with dominant negative (DN) SMAD3 variant in the MH2 domain exhibited more major events (66.7% vs. 44.0%, P = 0.054), occurring at a younger age compared to those with haploinsufficient (HI) variants. The age at first major event was 35.0 years [IQR 29.0-47.0] in individuals with DN variants in MH2, compared to 46.0 years [IQR 40.0-54.0] in those with HI variants (P = 0.065).

evidence.text: A literature review and cohort analysis of 155 patients with pathogenic SMAD3 variants reported no significant correlation between variant type and the occurrence of an aortic phenotype.

source.title: Clinical and genetic data of 22 new patients with SMAD3 pathogenic variants and review of the literature
source.quote: We showed, herein, the absence of correlation between the SMAD3 variant type and the occurrence of an AP in patients.
